hypothesis: Adding a deterministic snapshot identifier and an optional expected-snapshot precondition will let hosts detect mid-session provenance rollover before mixing pages, while preserving the companion's offline read-only boundary.
heldOutChecks: every change page exposes a deterministic sha256 snapshot identifier
the identifier remains stable for identical evidence and changes when evidence changes
a matching expected snapshot continues to the exact next page without overlap or gaps
a mismatched expected snapshot fails closed before returning records
CLI accepts a matching snapshot precondition and rejects a mismatch with a nonzero exit
MCP exposes the snapshot precondition, rejects a mismatch, and the changes resource reports the same identifier

memoryDecision.ruvectorWasm: defer retrieval adoption until at least 100 sanitized provenance records support leakage-free exact, vector and fused comparisons; separately record the new supported MinCut WASM capability
memoryDecision.gnn: reject for the current corpus unless a held-out graph task demonstrates at least ten percentage points of task-success gain over exact filtering and a shuffled-graph control

forecast.prediction: Within 90 days, agent evidence and memory interfaces will increasingly expose content-addressed snapshot or receipt identifiers so caches, replay and audit can fail closed across state transitions.
forecast.falsifiableCriterion: By 2026-12-16, at least two primary agent-memory, MCP, or run-evidence implementations newly publish digest-, receipt-, or revision-bound snapshot metadata used for cache invalidation or replay verification.
